labels.name: Interpreter or Parser Injection
labels.description: Attacker-controlled data changes the grammar, executable structure, or directives consumed by an interpreter or parser instead of remaining a literal value. Evidence must identify the interpreted context and how input crosses its syntax boundary; malformed data that only crashes a parser, object reconstruction, and path selection are outside this family.

labels.name: Filesystem Resource Boundary Violation
labels.description: Attacker-controlled names, paths, archive entries, or filesystem links resolve to a file or directory outside the resource set intended for an operation. Evidence must show unauthorized filesystem target selection; object identifiers, network destinations, and merely dangerous uploaded content use other families.

labels.name: Unsafe Structured-Data Interpretation
labels.description: Attacker-controlled structured data is interpreted with object, reference, binding, or graph capabilities beyond the intended data-only contract. Evidence must identify the unsafe structured-data feature; ordinary parser crashes, query injection, and path traversal are outside this family.

labels.name: Network Destination Control
labels.description: Attacker-controlled network identifiers determine an unintended network destination or routing authority for a request, redirect, backend selection, or security-sensitive absolute URL. Evidence must trace input to that destination or authority; selecting a filesystem resource or injecting protocol syntax belongs elsewhere.

labels.name: Unsafe File Upload Acceptance
labels.description: An upload feature accepts attacker-controlled file content contrary to its intended content policy or trust boundary. Evidence must concern what file content the feature accepts; missing permission to invoke the upload, filesystem destination traversal, and resource-size abuse are separate mechanisms.

labels.name: Identity and Access-Control Failure
labels.description: The system fails to establish a principal, bind an authenticated session, authorize an action or resource, or verify the legitimacy of an authority-bearing request. Evidence must identify the failed access decision; obtaining privileges only as an impact of another mechanism is not enough.

labels.name: Memory Safety Violation
labels.description: The implementation accesses or manages storage outside the bounds, lifetime, initialization, pointer-validity, or object-type rules of a memory-unsafe runtime. Evidence must identify an invalid memory operation or an authoritative memory-safety diagnosis; a managed exception, parser rejection, or denial-of-service impact alone is insufficient.

labels.name: Resource Management Failure
labels.description: The defining defect violates a finite-resource bound, release obligation, or progress guarantee under attacker-reachable conditions. Evidence must identify the resource rule that fails; a crash caused by injection or invalid memory access is not independently a resource-management mechanism.

labels.name: Cryptographic Protection Failure
labels.description: A security control fails because of cryptographic primitive selection, key management, randomness, nonce handling, or peer-certificate validation. Evidence must identify the failed cryptographic property; plaintext exposure without an intended cryptographic control does not by itself satisfy this label.
